sources.entry: Racket: _Beautiful Racket: How to make your own programming languages with Racket_

summary.title: Beautiful Racket by Matthew Butterick
summary.one_liner: Learn to build your own programming languages with Racket by working through small language projects such as stacker, bf, jsonic, wires and basic.
keywords: build your own programming language tutorial
takeaways: Build a small language in about an hour using the stacker project.
Learn functional programming and macros by implementing funstacker and stackerizer.
Extend data formats and follow grammars through the jsonic and bf projects.
Implement a BASIC-style language in stages, from a basic core to closing the loop.
Understand core Racket concepts such as modules, syntax objects, macros, contracts and the #lang line.
summary.summary: Beautiful Racket is an online book by Matthew Butterick (version 1.6) introducing language-oriented programming with Racket. It is organized as a sequence of hands-on projects, starting with a stack-based language called stacker and progressing through funstacker, stackerizer, bf, jsonic, wires and basic. A reference-style section then covers Racket topics such as macros, modules, syntax patterns, contracts, parameters and the REPL, followed by a glossary and resources. The listing describes it as a tutorial for building your own programming languages in Racket.
